summary: Equivalent GUT triage receipts can use supported field aliases (organ/sourceOrgan, provenance/provenanceFingerprint, triageClassification/classification). Dynamic-decomposition v0.8 fingerprinted raw receipt shape after only transport-key projection, so alias-only schema variation could masquerade as multiple unique qualifying receipts.
risk: False receipt multiplicity could inflate provenance counts and weaken replay-contamination accounting even when downstream classification remained unchanged. Conflicting values across alias pairs also required an explicit conservative HOLD rather than implicit field preference.
resolution: Equivalent allowlisted aliases are canonicalized before replay identity. Alias-only duplicates therefore collapse to one qualifying receipt. If both names in an alias pair are present but disagree, decomposition returns HOLD with no facets; only value fingerprints are retained in conflict evidence.
provenance: Synthetic structural tests plus public GitHub Actions metadata only; no private Drive names, IDs, URLs, or source text are present.
boundary: Resolution is limited to the explicit schema-alias allowlist. It does not infer semantic equivalence for unknown fields, adjudicate source truth, install capability state, or authorize unrestricted self-modification.
